programs.name: ARISS-USA ISS Contact Proposals
programs.summary: A scheduled, voice-only contact of roughly ten minutes between your students and an ISS crew member, plus an ARISS Technical Mentor and an Educational Mentor to get the ground station and the education plan ready. No cash changes hands. Written for US schools and educational organisations; colleges and universities are not named in the eligibility sentence and K-12 dominates the awardee list.

amount.amountRaw: No cash. A scheduled ISS crew contact of approximately 10 minutes, plus an ARISS Technical Mentor who helps develop an Equipment Plan and an ARISS Educational Mentor. The applicant provides the ground station.

deadline.note: One window sentence rewritten quarterly at a stable URL. Application window published by the funder: opens 2026-07-01, closes 2026-09-30. The page prints the month and day and no year; the year is fixed by the contact period the same sentence names, January to June 2027.

programs.applyContact: If you have questions regarding the proposal process, please send an email to: education@ariss-usa.org

constraints.rawText: US schools and educational organizations may download the ARISS Proposal Form to submit a proposal to host an ARISS contact.

spec.note: US schools and educational organisations. Colleges and universities are not explicitly named in the eligibility sentence.

constraints.rawText: To maximize these radio contacts, the ARISS program looks for organizations that will draw large numbers of participants and integrate the radio contact into a well-developed education plan. Potential audience size: we are looking to engage an entire school or organization, NOT just a single classroom.

spec.note: An education plan reaching the whole school or organisation, not one classroom.

constraints.rawText: Because of the nature of human spaceflight and the complexity of scheduling activities aboard the ISS, organizations must demonstrate flexibility to accommodate changes in contact dates and times.

spec.note: The organisation must be able to absorb changes to the contact date and time.

constraints.rawText: Proposals from schools and organizations in the US are accepted during four proposal windows each year – one each quarter. Proposals are not accepted outside of the scheduled proposal windows.

spec.note: Four proposal windows a year; nothing is accepted outside a window.

constraints.rawText:
Educational proposals should include plans for students to:
study topics related to space technology, space exploration, or space research, and,
learn about communication, wireless technology, and radio science

spec.note: The education plan should have students study space technology, exploration or research, and learn about communication, wireless technology and radio science. ARISS writes "should" here and "must" for the flexibility requirement above.

fundingRestrictions: No cash is awarded. The ground station is the applicant's responsibility, though ARISS pairs the organisation with a Technical Mentor who helps develop an Equipment Plan.

obligations.sustainmentObligation: After the Equipment Plan is approved, the organization initiates their Education Plan, and preparations for the contact get underway.

sustainmentObligation.quote: After the Equipment Plan is approved, the organization initiates their Education Plan, and preparations for the contact get underway

programs.rawOtherText: SPARKI is named once on this page as a companion programme, and the proposal-window sentence is rewritten each quarter at a stable URL. Selection timing, in ARISS's words: 4 to 6 weeks after the close of the proposal window, organizations with approved proposals are sent a congratulatory email.

programs.name: NASA CubeSat Launch Initiative (CSLI)
programs.summary: Launch and deployment opportunities for CubeSats built by US educational institutions and non-profit organisations, museums and science centres included. NASA calls it a low-cost pathway to flight: the ride is the award, and the team designs, develops and builds its own hardware. There is no hardware funding, so budget for building the spacecraft separately. NASA has launched over 150 CubeSats through the initiative.

amount.amountRaw: a low-cost pathway to conduct scientific investigations and technology demonstrations in space

deadline.note: No dated window is published on the announcement page. The page states only a habit: CSLI's Announcements of Partnership Opportunity is typically released each August with proposals due in November. A habit is not a deadline, so nothing here is put on a calendar; watch the page for the announcement itself.

constraints.rawText: NASA's CubeSat Launch Initiative provides opportunities for CubeSats built by U.S. educational institutions, and non-profit organizations, including informal educational institutions such as museums and science centers to fly on upcoming launches.

spec.note: US educational institutions and non-profits, informal educational institutions such as museums and science centres included.

programs.name: NASA National Space Grant — 52 state consortia
programs.summary: Fifty-two independent state and territory consortia funding university students, faculty and teams. Per the research this is the most common real route to a campus ground station or a cubesat. Consortium-level student awards typically run $1,000 to $10,000 but are set consortium by consortium and are not published nationally. Shipped as a guided workflow with a state-keyed picker, not as a feed.

deadline.note: There is no national deadline and there never has been. Fifty-two consortia keep fifty-two independent calendars, rarely posted more than a semester ahead. Find your state's consortium and work to its calendar.

constraints.rawText: Applicants apply through their state consortium, normally via an affiliate institution, rather than to NASA directly.

spec.note: Apply through your state consortium, normally via an affiliate institution.

programs.name: IEEE MTT-S Chapter Support
programs.summary: Annual chapter activity funding from the IEEE Microwave Theory and Technology Society: $1,000 a year for a single-society MTT-S chapter and $500 for a joint chapter, plus a separate $500 seed fund for a workshop or symposium. The most RF-relevant money inside IEEE, and the requests are due by October 1.

amount.amountRaw: The amount of chapter activity financial support is $1,000 per year for single-society MTT-S Chapters or $500 per year for Joint Chapters which are associated with MTT-S.
amount.awardCountRaw: One activity-support award per active chapter per year.

deadline.note: RECUR n_fixed_dates tz=America/New_York dates=10-01 | All requests for MTT chapter funding must be received by October 1 or the chapter may be asked to make its application in the following year. No year is printed next to that date, and no opening date appears anywhere on the page: this is a deadline, not a window, and a late request is deferred rather than refused.

constraints.rawText: Chapters must have fulfilled all the following requirements for an 'active' status to be eligible for any one of the below funding programs: Minimum of ten (10) members; five (5) members for Student Branch Chapters.

spec.note: Ten members minimum, or five for a Student Branch Chapter.

constraints.rawText: Complete up-to-date Chapter Officer roster reported via vTools Officer Reporting. Minimum of two (2) reported technical meetings via vTools Events in the previous year, Chapters less than one-year-old are exempt from this requirement.

spec.note: Current vTools officer roster, and two reported technical meetings in the previous year unless the chapter is under a year old.

constraints.rawText: Before a chapter applies for MTT-S financial support they should apply for support from the IEEE Section to which that chapter reports. Sections receive a rebate for your chapter's past year's activities and the Section should support your current activities.

spec.note: Ask your IEEE Section first; MTT-S expects the Section to have been approached.

obligations.reportingObligation: Minimum of two (2) reported technical meetings via vTools Events in the previous year, Chapters less than one-year-old are exempt from this requirement.

reportingObligation.quote: Minimum of two (2) reported technical meetings via vTools Events in the previous year, Chapters less than one-year-old are exempt from this requirement

programs.rawOtherText: In addition to the chapter activity support above, MTT-S offers $500 seed money per chapter for a workshop or symposium, on condition that an IEEE MTT-S membership booth is present at the event, and up to $2,250 a year of Chapter Officer travel support to attend a Chapter Chair Meeting.

programs.name: IEEE MTT-S Undergraduate Scholarships and Graduate Fellowships
programs.summary: MTT-S runs undergraduate scholarships and graduate fellowships for students working in microwave theory and technology or a directly related RF field, alongside its chapter funding. An amateur licence is not required. Recorded so a ham student in an EE programme knows they exist — but the MTT-S page this record was built from only links to them, so no amount, no count, no deadline and no eligibility rule of the funder's own is recorded here. Everything above is GrantSpotter's reading, not MTT-S's text.

deadline.note: No deadline is published on any captured page. The October 1 cutoff on the chapter-support page governs CHAPTER funding requests and must not be assumed to govern these student awards; the two are separate programmes.

programs.name: IEEE Student Branch Annual Rebate
programs.summary: A rebate paid to IEEE Student Branches that file their Annual Plan. The plan is due 15 March and filing it is what qualifies the branch: "Submitting an Annual Plan is required to qualify for a Student Branch Rebate." The rebate schedule itself is not published on the page IEEE points branches at, so no amount is recorded here — ask your branch counsellor for the current figures.

amount.awardCountRaw: One rebate per branch per year.

deadline.note: RECUR n_fixed_dates tz=America/New_York dates=03-15 | Student Branch Annual Plans are due 15 March. No year is printed next to that date and no opening date appears anywhere on the page, so this is a deadline projected forward as a rule, not a window IEEE published.

constraints.rawText: Submit your Branch's Annual Plan through vTools Student Branch Reporting. Submitting an Annual Plan is required to qualify for a Student Branch Rebate.

spec.note: A recognised IEEE Student Branch that has filed its Annual Plan through vTools.

obligations.reportingObligation: Submitting an Annual Plan is required to qualify for a Student Branch Rebate.

reportingObligation.quote: Submitting an Annual Plan is required to qualify for a Student Branch Rebate.

programs.name: Yaesu System Fusion DR-2X Repeater Program
programs.summary: A limited-time purchase programme, not a grant: Yaesu USA offers the DR-2X dual-mode repeater at a program price through August 31st, 2026. Yaesu states two prices, $1,450.00 and $1,860.00, and does not say what distinguishes them, and states no eligibility requirement of any kind. The application is a dated fillable PDF whose address changes every time a new window opens.

amount.amountRaw: The new program price is either $1,450.00 or $1,860.00.

deadline.note: Irregular windows announced by the funder with no fixed schedule. Application deadline published by the funder: closes 2026-08-31. Yaesu states no opening date; the fillable form's filename names months without day numbers, so only the close is dated.

fundingRestrictions: No money is granted. This is a purchase: the buyer pays the program price.

programs.name: Campus Student Government / student activity fee funding
programs.summary: Your own campus student government is one of the two most reliably winnable sources of money for a collegiate radio club, and the one no aggregator can index: roughly 4,000 campuses with independent rules on Qualtrics, CampusGroups, Presence and Engage. Every campus expects a registered student organisation in good standing, but no campus's own wording is recorded here. Shipped as a playbook rather than an opportunity, because there is nothing here to poll; the playbook itself is in the writing desk.

amount.awardCountRaw: Varies by campus; FSU caps event and travel requests at three per organisation per fiscal year.

deadline.note: Hybrid on most campuses: rolling event and travel requests with a lead-time requirement — six weeks at FSU — plus one annual activity-and-service budget cycle. Ask your own student government for both calendars; no national date exists and none is projected here.

fundingRestrictions: Capital equipment is frequently barred outright by student-activity-fee rules. A radio often cannot be bought with this money directly.

trust.staleMirrorWarning: One campus's figures, FSU's, kept as a representative example and nothing more: programming up to $3,000 and up to $5,000 in extraordinary cases, travel $250 per student and $5,000 per organisation, a development fund up to $300 per fiscal year, and a six-week lead time. They are not your campus's rules. Read your own student government's allocation manual before you budget anything.
